free_tier.stated: EUR 2.60/month for KVM-XS in Velbert, Germany, after coupon LEB35: 4 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 25 GB disk, 1 TB traffic, 2x 10 Gbit shared uplink, 1 IPv4 and a /64 IPv6, EUR 26.00/year on the annual term after the same coupon. The post's table prices KVM-M at EUR 9.10/month for 12 GB, 4 vCPU and 75 GB, KVM-L at EUR 11.70 for 18 GB, 6 vCPU and 100 GB, and KVM-XXL at EUR 22.75 for 32 GB, 10 vCPU and 250 GB, all with 1 TB traffic. Every figure in the table is a post-coupon figure; the pre-coupon list price is not printed.

egress.terms: 1 TB a month on every plan in the offer table; no overage price and no post-allowance throttle stated

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: the vendor runs a looking glass at lg.velohost.de with a 50 MB test file; no API or CLI is documented on the page read
record.chaining: EUR 2.60/month for 4 GB and 25 GB with 1 TB of transfer is the cheapest 4 GB row among documented hosts and the only one whose vendor says it owns its hardware and added a second German site; 1 TB a month is the reason it is a worker and not a mover, and the coupon is what makes the price, so the record is only valid while LEB35 stands

limits.value: 1 TB a month on every plan in the table, including the 32 GB one, so the byte allowance binds long before the 2x 10 Gbit shared uplink does. No overage price and no post-allowance throttle are stated on either page read, and the post does not say whether the counter resets monthly or on the billing period.

record.limits_note: 1 TB a month on every plan in the table, including the 32 GB one, so the byte allowance binds long before the 2x 10 Gbit shared uplink does. record.binding_note: 1 TB a month on every plan in the table, including the 32 GB one, so the byte allowance binds long before the 2x 10 Gbit shared uplink does. evidence.proved: third-party offer post, published 2026-10-13, quoted from its table: 'KVM-XS 4GB RAM 1x vCPU 25GB disk 1 TB Traffic 2x 10 Gbit (Shared) 1x IPv4/64 IPv6 Coupon: LEB35 2,60 EUR/month (after promo code) 26,00 EUR/year (after promo code)'; the three larger rows carry the same '1 TB Traffic'; host nodes are '1x AMD EPYC 7C13' and '2x AMD EPYC 7402P' with '512 GB RAM' and '2x 4TB NVMe-SSD'

the vendor homepage was read and carries no KVM plan table or price at all: it shows a German navigation page with a KVM product link to velohost.de/kvm-ipv4.php and a domain search form, so no figure on this record could be corroborated first-party

record.notes: Every price is post-coupon and the post prints no list price, so the pre-coupon rate and the renewal rate are both unverified: the post says 'Use promo code LEB35 to get 35% off all KVM plans starting from KVM-XS' and does not say whether the code is recurring or first-term only. Unverified: the KVM page at velohost.de/kvm-ipv4.php, which the homepage links and which this category did not fetch, and whether LEB35 survives renewal. The euro sign was dropped by the text extractor on the post table, so the currency is taken from the post's title line rather than from the garbled glyph.

record.category: vps (hosted, Germany, KVM, IPv4 and IPv6)

free_tier.stated: No free plan. KVM-XS is 4 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 25 GB disk and 1 TB traffic at EUR 2.60 a month or EUR 26.00 a year after the promo code LEB35 (35 percent off); the post prints no list price.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a rented server, not an object store

retention.stated: not applicable: a live server, not stored bytes

egress.terms: 1 TB per month is the reference value of the terms where no other volume is agreed; the terms reserve EUR 5.00 per started extra TB, and temporary suspension on excessive use of the agreed or fair-use traffic
egress.free_allowance: 1 TB per month on every KVM plan in the offer post, paid, no free tier
egress.price_per_tb: EUR 5.00 per started terabyte over 1 TB, at the vendor's discretion

record.interface_detail: a KVM guest with full root access, ordered through the provider's WHMCS store
record.tooling: any SSH client; the provider's client area
record.chaining: a plain KVM guest with one IPv4 address and a /64 IPv6 subnet on a shared 2x 10 Gbit uplink; outbound TCP 25, 465 and 587 are blocked by default and every other port is not stated as filtered

limits.value: 1 TB per month, then EUR 5.00 per started extra terabyte or a temporary suspension at the provider's choice
outbound TCP ports 25, 465 and 587 are blocked by default and opened only after a review in the individual case

record.binding_note: 1 TB per month is the only byte ceiling and the terms put a price (EUR 5.00 per started TB) and a suspension right on exceeding it.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the registration page renders no form fields; the offer post lists PayPal, credit cards, bank transfers and crypto as payment methods, and no card, phone or ID requirement is stated on a page read

record.confidence_note: The traffic rule and the blocked mail ports are first-party terms; the plan table and the price come from a third-party offer post and are post-coupon figures. Inbound ports and UDP are not stated.
